chapter: Playing with Punch Miller and touring
title: Excursions to Chicago with Punch Miller
summary: Morris explains how he met Punch through Jack Carey, formed a travelling band, and played train excursions to Chicago.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And when did you start playing with Punch? When did you first meet Punch? Do you remember?

Well, I know Punch from playing with Jack Carey. And somehow or another they fell out or something and then I took Georgia Boy, that's the clarinet player and Punch and Walter Preston and Joe Gable. Then we went together and we was buying up everything we see and everything. We was in on one train going out on another. I believe we the first man started traveling, yeah, after Lewis left.
Going excursions mostly or what time?

Excursions, yeah. We had to play excursions all the way to Chicago. You wouldn't get there like now. Punch was playing then. As we go to Chicago, you sleep on that train that used to leave, we played from the IC, we played from the L&N. That train wouldn't get there until the next day, way in the day after that. Where did you play?
Did you have a little dance floor on one of the coaches?
On the coaches? Well, just the people selling and eating and drinking and you play in the coach.
Did you ever play in the baggage car and have dancing or anything like that?
No, there was no place to dance, it would be in the coach.
I heard something one time, somebody said they had dancing in the baggage car with the band

up there. No, they'd sell. They'd sell all the liquor and stuff in the baggage. But the band would be in half of a coach and they'd have their part, you know. It wouldn't give them no room to dance. I guess that's why they did that. Not the dancing, because they'd start a fight or something maybe, throw somebody out there. But after all, that's the way we used to play them in excursions at Chicago.
Then you'd stay there a few days before you came out there?
I'd stay there a few days and then we'd come out, yes.
